deep.reconstruction:
This folio holds three unrelated groups of computations. The first two belong to Riemann's P-function work; the third is potential theory.

(A) QUADRATIC TRANSFORMATIONS OF THE P-FUNCTION. The notation follows the next page. P(a,b,c,x) is a Riemann P-function with exponent differences a at x=0, b at x=1 and c at x=infinity. It is symmetrized so that the exponents are ±a/2, ±b/2, ±c/2 plus constant shifts. Because the exponents are symmetrized, P(λ,μ,ν) and P(-λ,μ,ν) are the same class; the page writes both down, and the previous page notes this explicitly.

Line 2 states the basic rule: P(λ, μ, -1/2, x) = P(λ, λ, 2μ, t), with t = (sqrt(1-x)-1)/(sqrt(1-x)+1).
- Inverting the substitution (my step): x = -4t/(1-t)^2. This is a degree-2 map.
- x=0 has two simple preimages, t=0 and t=∞, so each carries difference λ.
- x=1 has a single double preimage t=-1, so its difference doubles to 2μ.
- x=∞ has a single double preimage t=1, so the difference 1/2 doubles to 1 and t=1 is an ordinary point.
- So the new singular points are 0, ∞, -1 with differences λ, λ, 2μ.
- With u=-t this is the classical Gauss/Kummer formula F(a,b;a-b+1;u) = (1+u)^(-a) F(a/2,(a+1)/2;a-b+1;4u/(1+u)^2), where λ=b-a and μ=1/2-b.

Line 1 is the same rule with λ=α+β-1/2 and μ=α-β: P(α+β-1/2, α-β, -1/2, x) = P(α+β-1/2, α+β-1/2, 2α-2β, ·).

Line 3 apparently composes two such quadratic maps. P(λ,μ,1/2) can be lifted either to (2λ,μ,μ) or to (λ,λ,2μ). Hence P(2β-1, α-β, α-β) and P(2α-2β, β-1/2, β-1/2) are both equal to P(β-1/2, α-β, 1/2). The argument on the right is left blank.

(B) TOWARDS A CUBIC TRANSFORMATION. The note '= λ λ λ ; λ, 1/3, 1/3' poses the question of relating P(λ,λ,λ) to P(λ,1/3,1/3).
- This is the degree-3 case. Pull back by a cyclic cubic map that is totally ramified over the two points with difference 1/3. Those points become ordinary, and the third point splits into three points each with difference λ. Riemann–Hurwitz: 2+2 = 2·3-2.
- The values α=(3λ-1)/2 (struck out), β=γ=(-λ-1)/2 and δ come from the next page's dictionary 2α+1=a+b+c, 2β+1=a-b-c, 2γ+1=c-b-a, 2δ+1=b-a-c, taken with a=b=c=λ. They parametrize the Euler integral ∫ y^α (1-y)^β (1-xy)^γ dy.
- He expands the integrand's cubic: y(1-y)(1-xy) = y-(1+x)y^2+xy^3.
- He then tries substitutions (ζ, 1±ζz, Möbius images of the roots 0, 1, 1/x) to move the three branch points to roots with zero sum.
- He settles on roots 1, α, -1-α (here α is a new parameter) and computes z = (1-y)(α-y)(-1-α-y) = -(1+α)α + (1+α+α^2)y - y^3.
- Writing 1+α+α^2 = 3λ^2 gives z+α+α^2 = 3λ^2 y - y^3.
- He solves by Cardano: y=p+q with pq=λ^2 and -(p^3+q^3) = z+α+α^2 = z+3λ^2-1.
- With P=p^3/λ^3 and w=(z+3λ^2-1)/λ^3 one has P+1/P=-w. Then ((P+1)/(P-1))^2 = (P+1/P+2)/(P+1/P-2) = (2-w)/(-2-w).
- The critical values of the cubic are w=±2. Equivalently -w/2 = T_3(y/(2λ)), a Chebyshev cubic, which is conjugate to s→s^3. This is exactly the cyclic cubic map needed for (λ,1/3,1/3)→(λ,λ,λ).
- The computation stops at this point.

(C) ELLIPSOIDAL COORDINATES.
- Algebraic identity: u_λ^2(μ-ν)+u_μ^2(ν-λ)+u_ν^2(λ-μ) = μ(u_λ+u_ν)(u_λ-u_ν) + ν(u_μ+u_λ)(u_μ-u_λ) + λ(u_ν+u_μ)(u_ν-u_μ). The third term is only begun ('λ ∂u'). This form appears in the Dirichlet integral and Laplacian in confocal coordinates.
- Confocal quadrics: f(λ)=x^2/λ+y^2/(λ+b)+z^2/(λ+c)=1 defines λ(x,y,z).
- f(λ)-f(μ) = (μ-λ)[x^2/(λμ)+y^2/((λ+b)(μ+b))+z^2/((λ+c)(μ+c))]. This gives orthogonality of the confocal families.
- Implicit differentiation: f'(λ)λ_x + 2x/λ = 0, so (1/2)f'(λ)λ_x = -x/λ.
- Squaring and summing gives (1/4)f'(λ)^2 |grad λ|^2 = -f'(λ), because -f'(λ) = x^2/λ^2+y^2/(λ+b)^2+z^2/(λ+c)^2.

The fragments '(λ+μ+ν)/6' and '2λ-μ-ν < 3/2' are isolated conditions or inequalities with no visible derivation.
errors: δ is written as (λ-1)/2. The dictionary 2δ+1=b-a-c with a=b=c=λ gives δ=(-λ-1)/2. Only that value satisfies the constraint α+β+γ+δ=-2 implied by the next page. Either this is a slip or the sign is misread.

Line 2 places 2μ in the third slot. In the new variable t the singular points are 0, ∞ and -1, so the slot-to-point assignment is non-standard. The content is correct up to a Möbius relabelling (t→-t).

The Cardano normalization writes (p^3+1)/(p^3-1) where p^3/λ^3 is meant; this is exact only for λ=1. The numerator under the root appears to carry a stray '+1'. The correct relation is ((P+1)/(P-1))^2 = (w-2)/(w+2).

As transcribed, the last line reads (1/4 f'(λ))^2 |grad λ|^2 = -f'(λ), which is wrong. The correct statement is (1/4) f'(λ)^2 |grad λ|^2 = -f'(λ), equivalently (1/2 f')^2 |grad λ|^2 = -f'. This is probably a reading issue rather than Riemann's error.
Line 3 as transcribed, P(2β-1+α-β, α-β, x), has only two parameters. It is presumably P(2β-1, α-β, α-β, x), which makes it consistent.

results.modern_name: Quadratic transformation of the hypergeometric equation (Gauss–Kummer)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (1812/13), Kummer (1836); recast in P-function form by Riemann (1857)

results.modern_name: Composition of quadratic transformations (relation between two 'two equal exponent differences' classes)

results.what: Attempt to relate P(λ,λ,λ) to P(λ,1/3,1/3) by a cyclic cubic (Chebyshev T_3) substitution, solved by Cardano
results.modern_name: Cubic transformation of the hypergeometric function (Goursat's (1/3,1/3,ν)→(ν,ν,ν))
results.usually_credited_to: Goursat 1881 (systematic list); partial cubic cases arguably earlier (Kummer)

results.modern_name: Quadratic form of the Dirichlet integral in confocal ellipsoidal coordinates

results.what: Confocal quadrics f(λ)=1: orthogonality via f(λ)-f(μ) and |grad λ|^2 = -4/f'(λ)

deep.surprise_reason: The quadratic transformations are those of Riemann's own 1857 paper. The ellipsoidal-coordinate formulas are textbook material from Lamé and Jacobi. The only mildly notable item is that Riemann was setting up the cubic transformation (λ,1/3,1/3)↔(λ,λ,λ) through a Chebyshev/Cardano parametrization, a case systematized only by Goursat in 1881. It remains an unfinished sketch of a fairly simple cyclic cover, not a completed result.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'α-β, μ[?]' should read 'α-β'. The left side is P(α+β-1/2, α-β, -1/2, x), and the right side is P(α+β-1/2, α+β-1/2, 2α-2β, ·).
Line 3: 'P(2β-1+α-β, α-β, x)' is probably 'P(2β-1, α-β, α-β, x)', where the '+' is a misread comma.
'δ = (λ-1)/2': check whether the image shows (-λ-1)/2, which consistency requires.
Last line: '(1/4 f'(λ))^2' is more plausibly '1/4 f'(λ)^2', i.e. (1/2 f'(λ))^2.
'f(λ) - f(μ) = (μ-λ)' is incomplete on the page; a bracket factor follows implicitly.
'2-1/2-y' in the column of linear factors may be '2-1/x-y', matching the neighbouring entries '-1-1/x-y' and '-1+2/x-y'.
In the Cardano line, the denominator '-2 ± (z+3λλ-1)/λ^3' should read '-2 - (z+3λλ-1)/λ^3'.
